events.title: The recession reaches its low point
events.description: US economic activity reaches the turning point later identified by the NBER. That official announcement comes in July 1983.

events.title: A new missile-defense proposal
events.description: President Reagan announces a research effort to defend against nuclear missiles. It becomes a major Cold War debate.

events.title: Challenger is lost
events.description: Seven people die when the space shuttle breaks apart after launch. NASA pauses shuttle flights and investigates.

what_happened_next.text:
The economy began growing again after November 1982. People did not know the precise turning point on decision day. The organization that dates US recessions announced it in July 1983, after more evidence had arrived.

The years ahead brought very different news. Reagan proposed missile-defense research in 1983. In 1986, the Challenger disaster killed its seven crew members and led NASA to pause shuttle flights. These events mattered to people's lives without neatly predicting which investment would finish first.

All seven choices gained value in this window. Apple led, turning $10,000 into about $62,100. The international share basket also rose strongly. IBM gained too, but much less than Apple. Both were famous computer companies; that did not make their shares interchangeable.

An investor had to hold through each month to reach these ending amounts. The gains were not handed out evenly each year. Starting or stopping at a different date could also change the result, even for the same company.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: Recession, international debt and computer-company competition made the outlook uncertain.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: Each investment grew or shrank month by month. A share basket spread risk across many companies, but it could still fall sharply. Cash and bonds also paid income over the five years.
reflection.what_faded_away: A musical opening and a headline about stolen computer designs were memorable news. Neither told you the five-year ranking of these investments.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: No one could know the exact size or order of the gains in these seven choices. A gloomy starting point did not guarantee a poor five-year result.

hot_stock_outcomes.text: Apple introduced the Macintosh in January 1984. Pairing Macs with LaserWriter printers then gave businesses a new way to make polished pages. The Macintosh SE and Macintosh II widened the range in 1987; second-quarter sales that year rose 42%. These new uses and growing sales help explain the company’s progress during a strong five-year investment.

IBM’s annual profit rose about 20% in 1984, but its early lead in personal computers attracted cheaper rivals. In 1987 it launched the PS/2 to fight back. The investment ended well above its starting value, while the new product showed that even a computer giant had to keep defending its business.

Diet Coke became America’s leading diet soft drink by the end of 1983. Coca-Cola then changed its main drink’s formula in April 1985, angering many customers. The original returned in July. The company’s strong investment result covered both a successful growing brand and a famous product mistake.
